title: Above 1320px the header no longer lines up with the page grid
detail: <header class="shell"> spans the full viewport and .shell-bar only pads by --gutter. It has no --page-max limit. The footer sits in .grid-container, as the Site specimen's own header and footer do, but the shell does not. So above 1320px the header's wordmark and controls move out of the content column. Measured: at 1366 the header BRAGA starts at x=32 while the content and the footer BRAGA start at x=55. At 1440 it is 32 against 92, and the theme square ends at 1408 against a content edge of 1348. At 1920 it is 32 against 332, a 300px offset. This breaks the grid.css rule that content and rules start and end on column lines, and the header and footer wordmarks no longer stack. Suggested fix (Agent A, one line): give .shell-bar `max-width: var(--page-max); margin-inline: auto` and keep the full-bleed hairline on .shell. Lines up at 1024 and 768 (32 = 32).

title: A/B bench: the rule above "Power" is hidden and the gap below its label is doubled
detail: The Power group is <fieldset class="segmented rule-t"> (AbSampleSizeBench.tsx). A legend renders inside the fieldset's top-border band, and .segmented > legend is width 100%. The legend therefore paints over the 1px --rule, so no rule shows above POWER, while Inputs has one. Also, the 16px padding-top from `.bench-controls > .rule-t` lands between the legend and the strip. Measured at 1440: fieldset y=723 and legend y=723 (the legend sits in the border band); the gap from legend to strip is 32px for Power against 16px for Preset. The specimen (Site 06) has range → 16 → rule → 16 → POWER → 16 → control, and BUILD-BRIEF rule 10 says to keep the specimen's spacing. The confusion matrix is not affected: its groups use p.label.rule-t. Fix options: wrap the fieldset in an element that carries .rule-t and the padding, or open Power with a p.label.rule-t as Inputs does.

title: theme-color metas stay on the OS values after a reload with a stored theme
detail:
This is still present; it is already in the integrator's open list (B). Steps: light OS, stored bk-theme=dark, then reload. The page renders dark (body rgb(25,26,29), color-scheme dark), but the metas stay ['#E4E6EA', '#191A1D']. The light-media meta applies, so the browser UI is light around a dark page until the first click; after a click both metas are set to #191A1D. D-024 asks for theme-color per theme. Fix: have the toggle script's start-up path, which already calls label(current()), also write colors[current()] into both metas.
[also reported by another lens:] D-024 requires a theme-color per theme. Only the click handler of the inline toggle rewrites the two metas. The pre-paint script sets data-theme but leaves the metas alone. With the OS in light mode and bk-theme=dark stored, the page renders dark while the light-media meta still says #E4E6EA, so the browser chrome is light over a dark page. The integrator already lists this as open from Agent B. It is confirmed here.
[also reported by another lens:] D-024 wants a theme-color per page theme. The pre-paint script (Base.astro:37) sets data-theme but leaves the metas alone; only the click handler (line 52) rewrites them. Measured in Chromium:
- OS light with stored dark: the page is dark, the light-media meta still reads #E4E6EA.
- Light chosen under OS dark, then reload: the page is light, the dark meta reads #191A1D.
- No stored choice and the OS switches to dark while the page is open: the page turns dark, but the button's aria-label still ends "· Light" (no matchMedia listener).
The two theme-color hexes are also copied by hand into Base.astro:42–43 and src/pages/index.astro:25–26. The css lint exempts any line containing "theme-color", so a token change will not reach them.

title: Tool verdict sentence is not in a live region; the KPI live region announces bare numbers
detail:
`

` (AbSampleSizeBench.tsx:195, ConfusionMatrixBench.tsx:135) is the primary readout and changes on every input. title: Confusion-matrix verdict can print shares summing to 101%, and claims "every positive is flagged" when there are none
detail:
Shares are rounded independently (lines 174–175). With Churn and costFP 3, costFN 10 the costs split 62.5 / 37.5, and the verdict reads "63% from the 20 churners missed, 38% from the 40 false alarms" (101%).
